absent: Definition, field layout and size of the table entry type and expansion of the table construction macros.
Runtime consumers of these tables, lookup order, default handling for unlisted bits and update timing.
Locking, concurrency, initialization, entry points and caller contracts.
Numeric values of trap bit masks, feature identifiers and reserved masks.
Behaviour on dynamic guest feature changes and interaction with host capability sanitisation.

findings.text: This configuration unit pairs groups of fine grained trap control bits with the guest architecture feature that makes them meaningful, using read only tables keyed by control register and local per VM predicates for composite feature conditions.

Local predicates test the guest view of ID registers through per VM helpers, combining fields with negation, conjunction and disjunction to cover split encodings such as nested virtualization levels, RAS versions, CSV2 levels, error syndrome pairs, mixed endian modes, MTE async, branch and pointer authentication variants, VMID width and EL3 absence.
PMU version predicates accept only an exact version encoding and explicitly reject the implementation defined encoding, with separate predicates for several PMU minor versions.

The large physical address predicate requires 52 bit support or lack of granule support across stage one and stage two 4K and 16K granule fields, using a helper that treats stage two support as present when either encoding indicates it.

Secondary capability checks for SME, SPE and TRBE read host system registers for SMPS, FDS, FnE and MPAM instead of the guest view, with embedded notes that they should later consult the guest registers if KVM gains support for those extensions.

Read and write traps for general EL1 system registers are gated by owning extensions such as AIE, stage one and two permission overlays and indirection, THE, SME, GCS, LS64, RAS, GICv3, LOR and pointer authentication, while a large baseline set of core EL1 registers is marked never subject to fine grained undef under baseline execution state.

Read and write traps for debug, trace and performance controls are gated by owning extensions such as SPE, BRBE, trace, PMU, TRBE, TRF, double lock, AMU, SPMU and newer PMU and debug extensions, with core debug registers marked never subject to fine grained undef.

Traps for system instructions including address translation, cache and TLB maintenance, speculation barriers and GCS and BRBE operations are gated by owning extensions, with core maintenance and exception operations marked never subject to fine grained undef.
All activity monitor read trap bits for counters, type registers and enables share a single gate on the activity monitor extension.

Extended hypervisor control bits are individually gated by their owning extensions including nested virtualization, masked system registers, pointer authentication, FPMR, GCS, 128 bit system registers, error syndromes, double fault, D128, THE, SCTLR2, TCR2, MOPS, CMOW, NMI, SME, XS and LS64 variants, with dedicated entries forcing reserved zero and one patterns.

Base hypervisor control bits are gated by 32 bit support, absence of EL3, a broad baseline execution state set, plus AMU, SCXT, EVT, LOR, MTE, nested virtualization, pointer authentication, RAS, RME, stage two write back, WFE trapping and E2H handling, with dedicated entries forcing reserved patterns.
System control register two bits are gated by double fault handling, error syndrome enables, 128 bit support, pointer authentication and CPA2, with dedicated entries forcing reserved patterns.

The unit recognises fine grained trap controls for general registers, debug registers, instructions, activity monitors, second versions of those controls, plus hypervisor controls and system control two, as the configuration identity set for this dossier.
Reserved handling uses never trap, always reserved one, reserved when E2H and forced reserved zero or one markers to constrain baseline and reserved bits.
